title: Best ai workflow for 2d topdown game
author: FamiliarEstimate6267
selftext: What would be the best ai workflow for a 2d top down preferably pixelated game.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
you probably want to spend the time to prepare the graphic assets first

get the grid system working before anything else

if it is your first project, I would suggest just using an existing pack and then just ai generate some additional stuff as needed

comments.author: Southern_Charge5794
comments.body:
If you want something big and not proof of concept it is better to learn engine of choice. Cause it sounds like you wanted to vibe code the whole game and at least for me it is a dead end. I am using Godot and with my dev background I see how very suboptimal solutions are there that leads to a lot of tech debt that is impossible to maintain, bugs and etc.  
My workflow is kind of specification driven development where you work on implementation plan and decompose it

replies.author: FamiliarEstimate6267
replies.body: I started using godot as well and have been enjoying it

comments.author: Foreign-Bluebird-901
comments.body:
I just built a HTML ecosystem catalog and editor that allows me to keep track of stats for all the units in a sort of gba pokemon final fantasy game, and it exports a JSON that can communicate with the WORLD editor, battle test harness, and map test harness (all in the world editor in GODOT also made by claude) I then handed the file back to claude and we outlined the vibe of the units and their balance etc etc and claude provided a JSON to put back into the editor with lots of basic template stuff. 

The World editor is still under construction, its got a lot of basic features but at the end it will basically have the same capabilities, it can export data that will be able to be read by claude and claude can provide updated versions to then be loaded back in as nessecary if needed while all the manual controls are still available to be used as a layman.



https://preview.redd.it/c5u5d4zgvt8h1.png?width=1366&format=png&auto=webp&s=d81af41cf219cd30401e16e2b1e5741ca5c3c71f

replies.author: Foreign-Bluebird-901
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/l411ifacwt8h1.png?width=1366&format=png&auto=webp&s=cd66c9ee2905829e33156b675672d01e9f2052be

The world editor is still pretty rudamentary but I plan that it will have a lot more placeholders, the ability to make new types of terrain etc, and make a library of features and anything else governed by the world editor similar to the catalog in the ecosystem editor. all of this data can and will later be used by probably a procedural generator, and ideally I will add the ability to preview graphics etc etc. Ideally these tools will be enough for basically any motivated lay man to be able to make a top down grid game, either just manually (hard) or possibly with AI assistance to simply use these tools and then do the work of applying ones own graphic and audio assets and putting it all together into a final game (which may be something I make a final editor for to give control. 

My logic in all this, I don't know a lick about coding, so I need editors where at least I can read stuff in human format to understand and observe what the AI is making, but also I can tweak or write things myself without any programming knowledge.
